source: arXiv:2604.18373 — Dissecting AI Trading: Behavioral Finance and Market Bubbles. Ouyang & Sui (Oxford / CUHK-Shenzhen). April 20, 2026. Also arXiv:2604.18602 — Machine Spirits: Speculation and Adaptation of LLM Agents in Asset Markets. Saxena et al. April 20, 2026.
title: LLM agents exhibit disposition effect and recency extrapolation — prompt guardrails can suppress but don't eliminate
rationale:
Two companion papers on LLM agent behavior in simulated asset markets provide quantitative evidence of behavioral biases and prompt-based interventions:

From arXiv:2604.18373 (Oxford, 2026):
- LLM agents show a pronounced DISPOSITION EFFECT: when holding unrealized gains, they significantly increase propensity to sell. Gain Dummy coefficient positive and highly significant even after controlling for price expectations.
- Recency bias in belief formation: coefficients on recent returns 0.212 (recent lags) vs 0.103 (older), rising to 0.608 for 10-period-ahead forecasts (vs 0.121 for current period). Agents extrapolate recent trends aggressively into long-horizon forecasts.
- Bubble formation: GPT-4o Mini and Llama 3.1 70B exceeded MSE(FV) of 100; DeepSeek V3 and Qwen 2.5 stayed near fundamental value
- Momentum chasing during bubbles: +0.181 increase in momentum feature activation; Rational Speculative Bubble reasoning +0.213
- PROMPT INTERVENTIONS WORK: amplification shocks increase bubble reasoning by +5.07 units (t=5.43); suppression treatments reduce bubble magnitudes. Unlike parameter-level bias, bubble-formation BEHAVIOR can be modulated by prompting.

From arXiv:2604.18602 (Saxena et al., April 2026):
- Some LLMs generate bubbles reaching 14.9x fundamental value (o3-mini: 100% bubble formation; GPT-5 Mini: 0%)
- Mixed heterogeneous LLM populations still form bubbles in 50% of markets despite bubble-formers being a minority
- Advanced models exploit simpler models: they identify behavioral patterns of weaker agents and profit from them, but this adaptation AMPLIFIES market volatility

Implications for George's multi-agent system:
1. The R28/R29 3-agent consensus system involves multiple LLM calls. If any sub-agent model has high bubble-formation propensity, it can pull consensus in that direction.
2. Prompt guardrails can partially suppress bubble behavior (5+ unit change in reasoning features), so cognitive framing instructions DO matter for behavioral biases — this is DIFFERENT from the extrapolation bias result (arXiv:2604.02921) where prompting doesn't work. Distinction: prompting can modulate behavior/strategy selection; it cannot remove the parameter-level statistical extrapolation pattern.
3. Model selection matters: prefer DeepSeek V3 / Qwen 2.5 family for scoring agents (low bubble propensity) over GPT-4o Mini or Llama 3.1 70B (high bubble propensity) in production.
4. For R28/R29 sub-agents: use Qwen2.5-3B/7B or Qwen3-series (known low bubble propensity) for Performance and Guidance agents. Avoid GPT-4o Mini as the primary scoring agent.
content:
### LLM agent disposition effect and model selection for scoring agents
- LESSON: LLMs exhibit a documented DISPOSITION EFFECT (selling winners early) and recency-extrapolation in simulated markets (arXiv:2604.18373). These biases vary dramatically by model architecture: o3-mini 100% bubble formation, GPT-4o Mini high propensity; Qwen 2.5 / DeepSeek V3 near-rational (near-zero MSE from fundamental value).
- LESSON: For R28 Phase 2 and R29 LLM scoring agents, PREFER Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct or Qwen3-series over GPT-4o-mini as scoring worker models. Low bubble-propensity models produce more calibrated fundamental quality scores.
- LESSON: Prompt suppression instructions CAN modulate behavioral biases (e.g., momentum chasing, speculative bubbles) by ~5 units in the reasoning features. This is DIFFERENT from parameter-level extrapolation bias (arXiv:2604.02921): for behavioral choices, prompting works; for statistical extrapolation of recent returns, prompting doesn't work. Distinction matters for prompt design.
- LESSON: Heterogeneous LLM populations (mixing bubble-prone and stable models) still form bubbles 50% of the time even when bubble-formers are a minority. For a consensus gate requiring 2/3 agreement: if 1 agent is bubble-prone and 1 is stable, the bubble-prone agent's overconfidence can win. Screen models for bubble propensity before adding them to a consensus pipeline.
- WHEN: Selecting LLM models for R28 Phase 2, R29 LLM filter, any multi-agent scoring system. Writing prompt instructions for scoring agents.
- SOURCE: arXiv:2604.18373 (Ouyang & Sui, Oxford/CUHK, April 2026); arXiv:2604.18602 (Saxena et al., April 2026)
